questions.q: Why is a fixed asset capitalized instead of expensed immediately?
options: Because its benefit spans more than one accounting period, so the cost is recognized gradually
Because the vendor requires it
Because it is always below the capitalization threshold
Because the General Ledger cannot process expense journal entries
questions.explain: Capitalizing spreads the cost of a multi-period benefit across the periods it's used, via depreciation, rather than hitting the income statement all at once.

questions.q: What determines whether a purchase is capitalized as an asset or simply expensed?
options: The asset's physical location
The company's capitalization threshold
Whether the vendor is new or existing
The General Ledger calendar
questions.explain: Companies set a dollar threshold below which a purchase is expensed regardless of its useful life; above it, the purchase is capitalized.

questions.q: Put the asset lifecycle stages in the correct order.
options: Retirement, Addition, Depreciation, Adjustment, In Service
Addition, In Service, Depreciation, Adjustment/Transfer, Retirement
Depreciation, Retirement, Addition, Adjustment, In Service
In Service, Retirement, Addition, Depreciation, Adjustment
questions.explain: The lifecycle runs addition, then capitalization/in service, then depreciation, then adjustments or transfers while in use, then retirement.

options: The original purchase price only
The proceeds received when an asset is sold
Cost minus accumulated depreciation
The capitalization threshold for a category
questions.explain: Net book value is what remains to be depreciated: the asset's cost less the accumulated depreciation taken against it so far.

questions.q: How does an invoice line in Payables become a candidate for an asset addition?
options: It must be approved by the asset's manufacturer
It is coded to an asset clearing account instead of an expense account
It is automatically flagged once the invoice is over 30 days old
Every Payables invoice becomes an asset by default
questions.explain: Only invoice distributions coded to an asset clearing account flow into Assets as mass addition candidates; expense-coded lines never do.
